name: Frontiers of the Roman Empire – The Danube Limes (Western Segment)
description: Along nearly 600 km of the Danube, through Germany, Austria and Slovakia, this stretch of the Roman Empire's northern edge survives as a chain of ruins. You can find legionary fortresses and their towns, small forts, temporary camps and old roads. Because the riverbanks were boggy, the Romans built no continuous wall here. Instead they placed watchtowers and stone-walled forts to suit the landscape.
